Cannabis certificates of analysis report acidic and neutral cannabinoids separately, and the headline "total THCV" a lab prints is a decarboxylation-weighted sum. If that computed number and the raw panel underneath it ever disagree, a static page just prints whichever line came first — a customer or a regulator has no way to know.

StrainChain's genetics dossier for a cultivar recomputes every total from the certificate's raw values at render time, instead of storing and trusting a number a lab (or an earlier version of the page) typed once. If a certificate's own published total and StrainChain's derived total disagree, the page shows that discrepancy directly rather than picking a side.

Lineage between cultivars works the same way: each parent/child relation is tagged as confirmed in writing, inferred, claimed, or no evidence at all — an inferred relationship is never rendered as a confirmed one.

Each cultivar page also carries a checksum computed from the certificates and lineage shown on that page, reproducible from the published bytes. We're explicit about its limits, right on the page: on its own it says what the record contains, not when it existed — it isn't a timestamp or a claim of priority, just something you can recompute yourself and check it matches.

StrainChain doesn't breed, sell, license or take an option on any genetics it records — that commitment sits on the passport page itself, not only in a policy document.

reddit.title: How should a cultivar genetics record handle a lab total that doesn't match its own raw panel?
reddit.body:
I work on StrainChain, a cannabis-provenance/genetics tool. The specific thing I want feedback on: a certificate of analysis reports raw cannabinoid values, then a "total THCV" or "total THC" line that's a decarboxylation-weighted sum. Most passport-style pages I've seen just print whatever total is on the certificate.

We changed our cultivar dossier to recompute every total from the raw values at render time instead, and if the certificate's own printed total disagrees with what we compute, the page shows that discrepancy rather than picking one number and hiding the other. Lineage between cultivars (parent/child crosses) is tagged the same way — confirmed in writing, inferred, claimed, or no evidence — and an inferred cross is never shown as a confirmed one.

Each page also carries a checksum over the certificates and lineage shown, reproducible from the published bytes — though we say plainly it's not a timestamp or a claim of who had a cross first, just something you can recompute and check hasn't silently changed.

For people who've dealt with breeder or cultivar records: does a discrepancy flag like this actually help, or is a mismatched total between a CoA and a computed total usually just lab rounding that nobody cares about?

https://strainchain.io/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=genetics-record-fingerprint&utm_content=a

Disclosure: I work on this project.
